headline: Indian Foreign Exchange Reserves Drop to $721 Billion From Peak
summary: India's foreign exchange reserves have declined by nearly $65 billion from their September peak to $721.016 billion, prompting warnings from academic researchers regarding RBI's $200 billion foreign currency non-resident exposure.
why: Foreign exchange reserves provide critical import cover and currency stabilization buffers for emerging economies. Sharp drops in gross reserves limit central bank intervention capacity during capital outflow cycles.

impacts.name: India
impacts.why: A $65 billion drawdown in reserves narrows the central bank's liquidity cushion against global currency volatility.
